newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU scientists say UK BSE gelatine ban should stay.
newsitem.headline: EU scientists say UK BSE gelatine ban should stay.

text.p: European Union scientists said on Monday that more research was needed into the transmission of mad cow disease to humans and that meanwhile a ban on British beef by-products, such as gelatine, should remain.

The scientists, headed by Swiss expert Professor Charles Weissmann, said the risk from infected animal feed and the efficiency of manufacturing processes in eliminating the Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) agent required further study.

"As long as this efficiency has not been demonstrated, the control of the nature, the geographical origin and the quality of the starting material remain the only means to assure the protection of public health," the committee said in a two-page opinion.
The EU imposed a worldwide ban on British beef exports in March after the British government caused a public health scare by disclosing that the fatal cattle brain disease could be passed to humans.
On June 11, the European Commission agreed to lift the ban on gelatine, a beef by-product widely used in food, cosmetics and medicinal products, if stricter heat processing methods were used.
But it subsequently learned that more research was needed into the safety of the new manufacturing methods and asked the committee of independent experts to assess the latest research.
British gelatine manufacturers, who have been using non-British raw meterials, have not requested permission to resume exports.
A European Commission official said the scientists' findings supported the EU executive's view that a ban on British gelatine should remain.
"If we were to be asked to lift the ban on gelatine we would not be able to do so," the official added.
Several experts have told a European Parliament committee of inquiry into BSE that the relaxation of the gelatine ban was premature and did not follow scientific advice.
